questionText: Should the ADR extension's autosaved answer drafts stay tracked in git?
draftText:
Option A, with some exceptions: Let's ignore `errors.jsonl` (which is used to report problems with the VSCode _ADRs for AI_ Manager which are collected here by the crew working on it), and let's ignore the `*.bak` files as redundant, but useful locally. I made a feature request with the VSCode _ADRs for AI_ Manager team, to create an efficient, and basic, "token redaction" heuristics in the drafts saved, based on the tokens we've encountered that other programmers are likely to encounter, and which we can update. That way, the drafts cache is not a vector for tokens to be leaked. (Tokens that are sensitive shouldn't be drafts or answers to ADRs/seeds.)

For the epistemic justification, beyond my eccentricity: In the same way as there is value as watching a model's thinking trace before the answer comes out, there is value to see the answers coalesce, be corrected, slow down, etc.. It is not a lot of data, it is in a dot folder which is invisible to users. This repository is one of the first few that we are building in public using this methodology, so, showing people how we think is part of the project.

questionText: When a model opens a porthole while you are typing elsewhere, may it take the keyboard?
draftText:
Ideally, Option C, yes — but I just did Spike 1, and it looks like we don't (yet?) know how to granularly control how the window is opened — at least not on macOS (it might be very different in Windows and Linux, and we should make a note to keep on the look out for those spikes in those OSes). So ideally Option C, and degrading gracefully to what is actually possible. If it's not possible to not take focus, I believe that is acceptable: The main reason I believe that is because of three things:
- I don't foresee models surfacing these pages frequently, it's an O(1) within a day;
- there is a very high, systematic, never amortized cost to search for these files, for opening them, then sending them to browser (whether internal or external) — the amortized cost of dismissing an occasionally unuseful floating window is, by comparison, very small
- in my own experience of the last year, it is very useful to have models have the ability to open a URL and grab focus and so imparting this ability to them is useful.
